_doc: Subset-decision register (roadmap P-SURF S7.2). Each entry attributes test262 core-incompatible cases to a recorded decision instead of an implementation. cluster_incompat.py applies each entry's predicate mechanically and reports attributed mass beside the gate numbers. Sign-off is delegated per takagi 2026-08-11 (decide-by-principles); entries remain takagi-vetoable.

entries.title: sloppy-only surface (noStrict-flagged cases)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: tr's language surface is TypeScript modules; module code is always strict (ES §16.2). The reference baseline bun runs .ts as ESM — the same always-strict surface. A noStrict-flagged case requires sloppy semantics for its assertions to hold and is not expressible as a TS module on either runtime: a language-definition boundary, not a missing feature. A sloppy/script mode would be a product-surface expansion foreign to TS; if ever authorized it becomes a post-v1.0 roadmap phase and this entry retires. Does NOT cover strict-semantics gaps where tr still leaks sloppy behaviour (e.g. the B.3.3 block-fn leak) — those stay implementation debt.

entries.title: source-phase imports proposal (ModuleSource / import source)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: source-phase-imports is a stage-3 proposal (import source / %AbstractModuleSource%), not a ratified ECMA-262 clause. The reference baseline bun (stable 1.3.14) rejects the `import source` syntax at parse, so no oracle exists on the baseline either; per the test262 discipline this entry records WHY rather than skipping silently: the phase semantics presuppose a module-source reification layer that tr's AOT compile-and-link model has no design for yet — a post-v1.0 roadmap phase, not an out-of-scope decision. The entry retires (cases return to the substrate queue) when the proposal is ratified or bun ships it, whichever is first.

entries.title: test262 staging directory (non-normative engine ports)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: test/staging is test262's incubation area, not normative corpus. Its contents are largely ports of engine self-tests — the SpiderMonkey sm/ tree dominates it, and those cases need sm/non262-*-shell.js harnesses that exist nowhere in the normative tree — exercising implementation-specific behaviour rather than ECMA-262 clauses, and they are staged precisely because they have not been reviewed for promotion. Attributing them records a CORPUS-scope fact, not a language-scope decision: there is no feature here that torajs declines to implement, which makes this entry categorically unlike SR-1/SR-2 (both of which do cut language scope). It is filed in the same register only because this is the one place attribution is computed mechanically. Retirement is automatic and per-case: when test262 promotes a staging case into the normative tree its path changes, the predicate stops matching, and the case returns to the substrate queue with no action needed here. NOTE the corollary, same shape as SR-1's: normative-tree cases that merely happen to resemble staging ones are NOT covered, and gaps they expose stay implementation debt.

entries.title: decorators proposal (demoted to Stage 2.7, zero engines shipping)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: The decorators proposal was moved BACK from Stage 3 to Stage 2.7 at the 2026-05-19 TC39 meeting, together with Decorator Metadata to keep the two aligned (minutes: 'Decorators moved back to Stage 2.7'). The stated reason is that it sat at Stage 3 for four years with ZERO engines shipping: SpiderMonkey holds a partial implementation it will not resume 'unless another engine ships first', XS declined outright, and browser-compat-data carries no decorators entry at all. bun 1.4 does ship them — through its own transpiler, not JSC — but per the test262 discipline (design-principles §5) bun shipping a thing is not what makes it orthodox; the spec is, and a demotion to 2.7 is the committee stating that the shape will still change. design-principles §7 forbids welding a shape-unsettled construct into class evaluation, which is the exact subsystem rotations 668-674 spent seven knives getting right. This is a timing decision, not a scope decision: TC39's own position is that decorators will be in the language eventually. Retires when the proposal returns to Stage 3.
